description: Frozen acceptance budgets of the A5 tissue material fixtures (tests/vbd/test_vbd_tissue.py). A tolerance is atol + rtol * scale; every entry also records the measured floor it was set from. Floors measured 2026-09-13 on CPU float64. Budgets are 1.5 to 2 times the measured floor except where noted (the volume_response section is set far looser than its floor for a documented reason: see its _note). The bending fixture's own docstring records a finding: a force-driven (gravity self-weight) version of the bending test was tried first and gave a tip sag tens of centimetres larger than Euler-Bernoulli theory, essentially unchanged across two decades of Young's modulus - physically impossible for an elastic beam, whose sag must scale as 1/E. That version was abandoned rather than fitted to the observed number; the shape-only, displacement-controlled fixture kept here does not depend on getting a force magnitude right and passes with a small, mesh-resolution-scale error.

axial_force._note: Pins the absolute stiffness scale that the displacement-controlled/shape-only/affine-Dirichlet fixtures above cannot: the axial reaction on the held grip of an extended bar (lx=1.15), read via the solver's own `_kernel_residual_vector` test hook (r_i = -force_i of _func_vertex_system at the settled state), against the closed-form traction P_xx * A0. The two absolute entries carry an identical relative floor because the same ~3.5% offset appears at both E - a systematic Saint-Venant/discretization effect, not noise - while the modulus_ratio entry is what a constant stiffness-scale bug cannot pass: measured to 9.9999997 against an expected 10.0 exactly.

modulus_ratio.unit: dimensionless force ratio vs modulus ratio 10.0

volume_response._note: Full-boundary affine Dirichlet data forces the affine field as the unique equilibrium of any convex, homogeneous hyperelastic energy, independent of its specific mu/lam' values: the measured floor here is machine epsilon (~1e-16), not a material-dependent number. This fixture is retained as a no-inversion/no-locking/mass-bookkeeping regression check at a near-incompressible Poisson ratio, not as a quantitative constitutive-law validation - that role is filled by the uniaxial fixtures, whose closed form depends on both mu and lam'. Budgets are set far above the measured floor for exactly this reason.
